STP Hub testing: from a trade ID to a bug

For Gabriella. Environment: UAT2. Logs: OpenSearch, index fidw-eu-bonds-uat2*.

1. Getting a trade to test

Source Who sends it What to do
Tradeweb You 1. Ask the Bonds EU team first (see IMPORTANT below). 2. In TeamCity, run [Bonds] Switch TWB Service between Environments with Switch to: UAT2. 3. Send the RFQ from Tradeweb to SAN3. It must appear in Darwin as an RFQ
TOMS Sergio Ask him in the chat. Say exactly what you need: bond or future; new, amend or cancel; any field that must be populated. He replies with the ticket number
Bloomberg Sergio Same as TOMS. BBG must also be switched to UAT2

Switching Tradeweb to UAT2 in TeamCity

IMPORTANT: before you touch anything in TeamCity, ask the Bonds EU team.

Tradeweb can only be connected to one environment at a time. If the Bonds EU team is using it in QA or UAT and you switch it to UAT2, you break their testing.

  1. Post in the Teams group Darwin | Bonds | QA or Darwin | Bonds | UAT: "Can I switch TW to UAT2?"
  2. Wait for someone to confirm.
  3. If nobody answers, send the same message privately to one of the Bonds EU QAs.
  4. Only switch after someone confirms.
  1. In TeamCity go to Darwin / SysOps / SLZ - NonProd / Services Management / EU Bonds / TransFicc Gateway.
  2. Click [Bonds] Switch TWB Service between Environments.
  3. Click Run (top right). The window Run Custom Build opens on the Parameters tab.
  4. Switch to: choose UAT2.
  5. Service name: click All. The 7 services are checked.
  6. Click Run Build.
  1. A build #UAT2-<number> appears at the top of the list.

A red #UAT2- build with Exit code -532462766 (Step: UP Service (DarwinEcsCli) / PowerShell) is normal. The switch still works.

If a #QA- or #UAT- build appears above yours, someone moved Tradeweb to another environment and your RFQs will not reach UAT2. There is a #QA- build every day at 05:45.

2. The 3 records of a trade

For every trade, find these 3 records, always in this order. This is the core of all STP Hub testing.

# Record What it tells you Search
1 XML What came into Darwin Event.Type: "TradeEvent" and "<trade ID>"
2 Payload What Darwin sent to STP Hub Event.Type: "PublishingStpHubEvent" and "<trade ID>"
3 ACK Whether STP Hub accepted it "<MessageId from the payload>"

If you have the 3, compare them against the story. If one is missing, go to "If any of the 3 records is missing".

Before you search

  1. In Confluence, open Darwin Home > Development: https://san-scib.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CIBFIIT/pages/148209979/Development.
  2. In the Bonds table, row UAT2, click the icon in the Kibana column. OpenSearch opens.
  1. Check you are in UAT2: the address starts with https://eu-bonds-uat2 and the index at the top left is fidw-eu-bonds-uat2*. Then go to Discover.
  2. Top right, set the time range so it includes the moment the trade was booked. Click the calendar icon and choose Last 24 hours. For an older trade, click Show dates and set the start and end date.
  3. Type the query in the search bar and click Refresh.
  4. Keep the quotes exactly as written below. Without them, IDs with $, . or _ return unrelated results.
  5. To read a result, click the arrow on the left of the row and open the JSON tab.

The Time column shows your local time. The @timestamp inside the JSON is UTC, 6 hours ahead.

Where the trade ID comes from

  • TOMS or Bloomberg: Sergio gives you the ticket number in the chat, for example 21027094.
  • Tradeweb: you copy it from Darwin. See "Tradeweb trades" below.

Below, each record has the general instruction first, and then a real example: TOMS ticket 21027094, booked by Sergio on 22 September. The screenshots are from that trade. To reproduce the example yourself, set the time range to 22 September 2026 with Show dates.

Record 1 of 3: the XML (what came into Darwin)

Event.Type: "TradeEvent" and "<trade ID>"

Open the result and read Event.TradeFeedXml. That is the message TOMS or the venue sent.

If there is more than one result, the trade was amended or cancelled: each amend or cancel adds its own events and they also contain the original ticket number. The field Event.LifecycleAction tells you which one is which: New is the original booking, Amend and Cancel are the changes. Open the one you are testing.

Example, 21027094: 3 results, because Sergio later amended this trade (new ticket 21027095). The original booking is the one with LifecycleAction "New", at 07:12:00.804.

The XML is long and you do not compare all of it. You pick the fields that feed the payload fields you are testing. This comparison is where bugs are found.

From the whole XML of this trade (screenshots below), these are the fields that were compared with the payload:

<SecurityIdentifierFlag>8</SecurityIdentifierFlag>
<BuySellCoverShortFlag>B</BuySellCoverShortFlag>
<CustomerAccountCounterparty>TELE</CustomerAccountCounterparty>
<AccruedInterestRepoInterest>92558.9</AccruedInterestRepoInterest>
<NumberOfDaysAccrued>328</NumberOfDaysAccrued>
<SettlementLocationAbbreviation>ST</SettlementLocationAbbreviation>
<InvertFlag>N</InvertFlag>

Each of these is checked against its payload field in "Then: compare the 3 records against the story". If a payload value does not match what the story says it should be, that is a bug.

Record 2 of 3: the payload (what Darwin sent to STP Hub)

Event.Type: "PublishingStpHubEvent" and "<trade ID>"

Open the result and read Event.Payload. If there is more than one result, open the one with the same ContextId as the XML you opened in record 1.

Copy the MessageId from the payload. The ACK does not contain the trade ID, so record 3 is searched by MessageId.

Example, 21027094: 2 results. The one with the same ContextId as the original XML (G39Y1319100021027094) is at 07:12:00.992. Its MessageId is 20d23472ced94447b643cced7164120c.

Record 3 of 3: the ACK (whether STP Hub accepted it)

"<MessageId>"

It returns the payload and the ACK. Open the ACK (Event.Type StpHubAcknowledgementReceived). Status: "OK" means STP Hub accepted the message. If you only get the payload, go to "If any of the 3 records is missing".

Example, 21027094: "20d23472ced94447b643cced7164120c" returns the ACK at 07:12:01.609 with Status: "OK".

Then: compare the 3 records against the story

Take each field of the payload you are testing, find its row in the story's mapping table, and check that the payload value is what the rule gives from the XML. If it is not, that is a bug.

Example, 21027094:

XML (record 1) Payload (record 2) Story
NumberOfDaysAccrued 328 AccruedDays 328 DWU-417
AccruedInterestRepoInterest 92558.9 AccruedInterest 92558.9 DWU-417
SettlementLocationAbbreviation ST Settlement.SettlementLocation "ST" DWU-417
InvertFlag N Settlement.InvertFlag "N" DWU-417
BuySellCoverShortFlag B Side "Buy" DWU-418
SecurityIdentifierFlag 8 Instrument.IdType "ISIN" DWU-418
CustomerAccountCounterparty TELE Counterparty.Glcs "TELE" DWU-418

All values match the stories and the ACK is OK, so there is no bug. Before 22 September, AccruedDays and AccruedInterest were published as 0 (bug DWU-616) and the two settlement fields as null (DWU-617). This trade was the retest of both.

Tradeweb trades

  1. Send the RFQ from Tradeweb and let it trade.
  2. In Darwin, go to Trades. The screen is called All Trades. Set the date filter to Today.
  3. Find your trade: Source System Name is Darwin, and Counterparty, Instrument Id, Price and Execution Timestamp match what you sent.
  4. Copy the value of the column Darwin Trade Id, for example TradewebEUGV$20260915.SAN3.EUGV.61.

Then search it in OpenSearch without the part up to the $, and with quotes:

Event.Type: "PublishingStpHubEvent" and "20260915.SAN3.EUGV.61"

Use the same text for record 1 (TradeEvent). For record 3, use the MessageId, as with TOMS.

A switch or a butterfly shows one row per leg, each with its own Darwin Trade Id. Search each leg separately.

If you cannot find your trade in the blotter, search the Tradeweb trades published in the last minutes (time range Last 15 minutes). The ID is in Event.TradeId:

Event.Type: "PublishingStpHubEvent" and Event.GatewaySource: "TRADEWEB_EUGV"

If any of the 3 records is missing

If you cannot complete the chain (input, payload, ACK), do not stop there. Run these searches to find where the trade stopped:

No payload (record 2). Darwin rejected its own payload before sending it:

Event.Type: "StpHubPayloadValidationFailed" and "<trade ID>"

Example, TOMS ticket 21027091 (22 September): "STP Hub payload validation failed for trade 'BloombergToms$21027091': field 'Mifid.Transparency' is invalid".

No ACK (record 3): the search by MessageId returns only the payload. STP Hub rejected the message (NACK). A NACK cannot be found by MessageId. Search all NACKs in the time range and find the one sent right after your payload (same minute):

Event.Type: "StpHubAcknowledgementReceived" and Level: Warning

Example, TOMS ticket 21027097 (22 September): Status: "ERROR" and the reason, /PostTradeEvent/Trade/Price/Yield: null found, number expected.

Any other problem. List every warning of the trade:

"<trade ID>" and Level: Warning

If none of these explains it, post the trade ID and what you found in the Darwin - STP Hub Validation chat.

3. From trade to bug: the full cycle (DWU-644)

  1. Sergio booked TOMS ticket 21023156 on 18 September.
  2. Fation checked the payload and wrote in the chat: "bug is the BrokerComission.Amount appears as null and the transactioncost in the toms message is informed".
  3. XML (record 1): <ClearingBroker>6ATE</ClearingBroker> and a transaction cost of 1200.0 EUR.
  4. Payload (record 2): "Broker":{"BrokerCode":"6ATE","BrokerCommission":{"Amount":null}}.
  5. Story DWU-417, mapping table: PostTradeEvent.Trade.Broker.BrokerCommission.Amount: "If TOMS fields ClearingBroker and <TransactionCost><Type>2</Type> are populated map <Cost>". There is a broker and a cost, and the payload publishes null. That is the bug.
  6. The bug was raised in Jira as DWU-644, parent DWU-434.
  1. After the fix, Sergio booked ticket 21027098 with a clearing broker and a cost on 22 September. The payload published "Amount":1200.0 and the ACK was OK. The retest comment was posted as PASSED and the bug was closed.

4. Raising the bug in Jira

Steps

  1. Open the Darwin Bonds US board in Jira and click + Crear at the top of the page.
  1. In the window that opens, check that the project is DWU and the type is Error (Bug in the Spanish Jira). Type the title of the bug and click Crear.
  1. A notice appears at the bottom left of the screen with the option to view the ticket you just created. Click it. The new ticket opens in its own window.
  2. In that window, fill in the ticket with the values in the table below.
  3. Post the link of the new ticket in the Darwin - STP Hub Validation chat.

What goes in each field

Jira field Value
Type Error (Bug)
Principal (parent) DWU-434, Post Trade & Allocations Feeds to STPHub
Title [Bug] <TOMS post-trade or Venue post-trade>: <field> is published as <wrong value>
Description Overview, Actual result, Expected result, as in DWU-644
Entorno (environment) UAT2
Evidence Screenshot of the payload, and of the XML if you compared against it
  • Include the story and the trade ID in the Overview.
  • Do not add steps to reproduce, explanations or open questions. Questions go in the chat.
